Oktober 1997 über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG; SR 955.0), particularly Art. 4 para. 1 let. b and Art. 6a; Geldwäschereiverordnung-FINMA (GWV-FINMA; SR 955.01), particularly Art. 2a regarding beneficial owner identification; FINMA Circular 2020/1 on money laundering supervision; Handelsregisterverordnung (HRegV; SR 221.411); Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 627 and Art. 708; Swiss Federal Act on the Implementation of the OECD Common Reporting Standard (SR 653.1) and the Tax Administrative Assistance Act (SR 651.1).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public with authority in the canton of registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; no apostille or consular legalization required for use in Switzerland

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the shareholder's jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the competent Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution of Foreign Corporate Shareholder approving incorporation and capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction with apostille or consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization by the competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and, where necessary, the Embassy of Switzerland

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Source of Wealth Form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Directors of the future Swiss company, countersigned by the Swiss incorporating officer/notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Switzerland for domestic execution; foreign signatures must be notarized and apostilled if executed abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and intended counterparties against the Swiss SECO sanctions and embargo lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions (as adopted by Switzerland), OFAC SDN list, and UK consolidated list. For politically exposed persons, enhanced due diligence per Art. 2a GwG-FINMA and FINMA Circular 2020/1 is required, including identification of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring for re-invoicing transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Index), www.zefix.ch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) for registration purposes. A non-Swiss transliteration or trade name may supplement the legal name provided it is not misleading and the legal name remains clearly identifiable. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name and must not imply a legal form, size, or activity that is inaccurate. The name must be consistent with the corporate purpose of the Aktiengesellschaft.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant must file a written objection with the competent cantonal commercial register office within 10 days of receiving the rejection notice. Should the objection be dismissed, the applicant may appeal to the cantonal administrative court within 30 days from the dismissal notice. Further appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court is available only if the case raises a significant legal question or fails within an enumerated exception. Fees for the appeal are levied under the cantonal legal tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not fully permissible as the sole registered seat. The company must maintain a physical, accessible registered office in Switzerland in accordance with Art. 627 of the Code of Obligations. For a commercial re-invoicing entity, the use of a serviced office with actual management presence, accounting records, and operational substance is expected; a mere letterbox address will be rejected by the commercial register and will fail income tax residency or anti-abuse substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first two operating years, reflecting Swiss cantonal tax authorities' enhanced scrutiny of newly incorporated, foreign-controlled AGs engaged in intercompany re-invoicing. Real inspection risk increases to above 40% if the entity does not maintain commensurate local substance (staff, premises, books, and bank account).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under cantonal tariff for official extracts and preliminary registration search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration fee for Aktiengesellschaft in the Commercial Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff calculated as 0.1% of nominal share capital with minimum CHF 100 and maximum CHF 1,000 (approx. USD 700 for CHF 100,000 capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication fee in Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fixed fee per insertion as set by the Federal Office of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association and incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss notary public in the canton of registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market notarial tariffs based on share capital and complexity; standard range CHF 1,200–2,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO due diligence and sanctions/PEP screening of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed legal and compliance service provider (advocate / fiduciary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark at an hourly rate of CHF 300–450, estimated one full day

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization fees for foreign corporate documents (Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, Board Resolution)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed government fees per apostille or consular legalization, average USD 80–120 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation of corporate documents and articles into an official Swiss language (if required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per word/page; estimated 20–30 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration preparation and internal corporate records establishment (share register and beneficial owner records)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard Swiss AG incorporation support, notarial annexes, and record book setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Arts. 632–632c (incorporation and minimum capital); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregister des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung), Articles of Association (Statuten), and Commercial Register registration application (Anmeldung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum share capital; at least 20% of each share's nominal value must be paid up, and at least CHF 50,000 in total must be deposited before registration; the deposit must be evidenced by a blocked-account confirmation from a Swiss bank and remains escrowed until the company is registered
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The board, having been appointed by the founder, resolves: 1. Share Subscription. The subscription of one thousand registered shares with a nominal value of one hundred Swiss francs each, fully covering the registered share capital of one hundred thousand Swiss francs, is accepted. At least fifty thousand Swiss francs have been duly paid into a blocked account in the name of the company before incorporation. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at the address recorded in the Articles of Association, Canton of Zug, Switzerland. 3. Officers. The persons named in the formation documents are appointed as director and authorised signatory with prescribed signature powers. 4. Governance. The board mandates filing of the incorporation application and confirms compliance with the Swiss Code of Obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Verification and Articles of Association Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug via Zefix commercial register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in Zefix to confirm the proposed company name is available and does not conflict with existing registrations, trademarks, or protected names. Draft the Articles of Association in accordance with Art. 626 OR, including company name, registered office, share capital, share classes, purpose (general trading and re-invoicing), and governance provisions. Submit the proposed name and articles for preliminary review if required by the notary.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name-search certificate
Identification of founder and initial shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, amend the proposed name to an acceptable variant and resubmit to the Commercial Register Office within the prescribed cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Deed and Blocked Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public in the Canton of Zug and a licensed Swiss bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder must appear before a Swiss notary to execute the public deed of incorporation and adopt the Articles of Association. Simultaneously, open a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company 'in formation' at a Swiss bank and deposit the required minimum capital of at least CHF 50,000. Obtain a banker's confirmation that the funds are irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the company until registration.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or identity card of each founder
Blocked-account opening forms and source-of-funds declaration
Bank confirmation of capital deposit and blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds or the notary requests amendments, provide the requested documentation and amend the deed or Articles of Association accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug through the EasyGov federal business portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal application for registration with the Commercial Register Office. Attach the notarized public deed, adopted Articles of Association, proof of blocked capital, declarations of acceptance of office from directors and signatories, and signature specimen cards. Pay the registration fee and ensure the application is signed by the authorized incorporator.
required_dossiers: Director and authorized signatory declarations of consent and signature specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register Office issues a query or deficiency notice, submit the required corrections or supplementary documents within the statutory cure deadline to complete the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Entry and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Commercial Register Office records the Aktiengesellschaft in the Commercial Register. The excerpt of incorporation is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), conferring legal personality and placing the company in the public register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication contains clerical errors, file a rectification request with the Commercial Register Office; any challenged registration may be appealed before the competent cantonal authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Ancillary Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA) for VAT; AHV compensation office and SUVA for social security; Cantonal Tax Office for profit/wealth tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Federal Tax Administration for VAT if anticipated turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or if voluntary VAT registration is elected. Register the company with the cantonal tax authority for corporate income tax, with the AHV compensation office for old-age and survivors’ insurance, and with SUVA for mandatory accident insurance. Obtain any commercial or domicile declaration if required by the Canton of Zug.
required_dossiers: Opening balance sheet or initial accounting documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or social security authority requests additional information, provide the requested confirmation letters or organizational information and re-file to avoid administrative penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None required for ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing and trade intermediation; the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) remains competent only for export-control or embargoed goods checks if applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license is prescribed for a pure re-invoicing trading company; commercial registration and VAT registration are the governing authorizations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical manufacturing or installation is established; no EIA is required for an office-only re-invoicing enterprise
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable given the absence of production or discharge activities; if the company trades responsibly sourced commodities, it must maintain due-diligence documentation required under Art. 964j OR and keep waste-transfer records for any returned or rejected goods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to an office-only re-invoicing operation; if a physical office is leased, the employer must obtain fire safety certification from the competent cantonal fire authority, verify structural load limits, and secure a workplace safety clearance through SUVA and the cantonal labor inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) — central authority for VAT, federal withholding tax and stamp duties; portal: www.estv.admin.ch. Direct federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax is administered by the Tax Office of the Canton of Zug (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung Zug / Amt für Steuern), portal: www.zg.ch/steuern.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Swiss AG must: (1) have its articles of incorporation notarized and be entered in the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug), which automatically generates the Swiss business identification number UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) from the Federal Statistical Office UID register; (2) file VAT registration with the ESTV Main Division VAT (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer) using form 1043 or the ESTV e-service when worldwide VAT-taxable turnover exceeds CHF 250,000, or voluntarily when below, obtaining a VAT ID of the form CHE-###.###.### MWST; (3) register for direct tax purposes with the Tax Office of the Canton of Zug using the UID, obtaining the tax account number for federal, cantonal and communal corporate income and capital tax; (4) register the company as a Swiss withholding tax debtor (Verrechnungssteuer) with ESTV for future dividend distributions. The UID is the mandatory statutory business identifier for invoicing and customs e-declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box regime; the AG is a resident capital company taxable on worldwide profit with territorial carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments. Available elections include: (i) VAT group election (Art. 21 MWSTG) treating closely linked enterprises as one taxable person; (ii) participation relief election (Art. 7 LIFD / Art. 70 DBG) exempting qualifying dividends and capital gains where the AG holds at least 10% of the share capital or an acquisition cost of at least CHF 1 million; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) in cantons offering the measure, including Zug; (iv) repayment of paid-in capital reserves without Swiss withholding tax instead of dividend distribution; (v) the Swiss hybrid mismatch rules (Art. 58a-h DBG, enacted under TRAF 2020) apply mandatorily and do not provide elective check-the-box or opt-out mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss Value Added Tax — Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Federal VAT Act (MWSTG/LTVA); no GST and no cantonal or communal sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 of worldwide annual turnover from taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies), aggregated at VAT-group level as of 1 January 2025 (previously CHF 100,000); voluntary VAT registration is permitted below the threshold; export supplies and certain exempt supplies with input tax deduction are disregarded for threshold computation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time electronic fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls or digital stamping; no tax-authority API pre-approval or digital stamp is required. E-invoicing is permitted under Art. 26a of the Swiss VAT Ordinance (MWSTV) if the system guarantees authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility; a PDF invoice sent by e-mail is accepted. Domestic invoices must contain the statutory elements of Art. 26 MWSTG (seller name/address, VAT ID 'CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST', date, description, net amount, VAT rate and tax per rate); the Swiss QR-bill with QR-IBAN is the mandatory payment slip for Swiss invoices. Invoice datasets must be made available to ESTV on request in an auditable format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 23 MWSTG, the 0% rate applies to: (a) goods transported or dispatched directly by the supplier from Switzerland to a foreign destination, to the supplier's own foreign warehouse, or on board aircraft or ships used in international traffic; (b) auxiliary services, including transport, loading, unloading and forwarding, directly connected to those exported goods; and (c) supplies whose place of supply is outside Switzerland under B2B recipient-based rules, which are outside Swiss VAT rather than zero-rated. A pure offshore re-invoicing hub whose goods never touch Swiss territory has no Swiss VAT nexus and needs no zero-rating claim. For goods dispatched from Swiss stock, zero-rating requires a Swiss Customs export declaration plus transport and delivery proof. International B2B services must be substantiated with the customer's foreign VAT ID and business-substance evidence; absent proof, ESTV deems the supply taxable in Switzerland at 8.1%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs export declaration (Zollanmeldung / SAD) submitted via e-dec or the FOCBS customs processing system, showing goods value, CN code, destination country and exporter UID
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or CMR international consignment note for road transport) evidencing physical dispatch from Swiss territory
Inward Remittance Certificate, or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advice, evidencing receipt of the foreign sales consideration
Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the export declaration and harmonized commodity codes
Proof of delivery (POD) or signed foreign warehouse receipt confirming arrival of goods abroad
Re-invoicing chain continuity file (purchase contracts, sales contracts, inspection certificates, correspondence) substantiating commercial reality
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV and the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) jointly audit export substantiation files. Deficient documentation triggers reassessment at the standard VAT rate of 8.1%, recapture of input VAT and statutory interest. Under Arts. 96-98 MWSTG, intentional tax evasion attracts a penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax; negligence attracts a penalty of up to one-third of the evaded tax; procedural violations attract fines of up to CHF 10,000. Qualified criminal fraud is referred to public prosecution. Retrospective clawbacks may extend over the full statutory limitation period (up to 10 years, with longer criminal prosecution periods for fraud). The exporter and any co-contractor who knew or should have known of the abuse are jointly and severally liable; fraudulent export zero-rating also triggers sanctions under the Customs Penalty Act and revocation of privileges in simplified export procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank), established under the National Bank Act (SR 951.11); sole issuer of Swiss franc (CHF) banknotes and authority for monetary policy, currently maintaining a low policy rate (sub-0.5%) reflecting disinflationary conditions. The SNB operates the SIC/SIC4 real-time gross settlement system and compiles external payments statistics but does not administer exchange controls. FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) supervises banking and AML/CFT conduct under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA, SR 955.0).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies full convertibility on both current and capital account operations, with no SNB or SECO authorisation required for cross-border fund movements. CHF is a freely floating G10 currency; exporters and re-invoicing hubs may contract and settle in CHF, EUR, USD or any other currency and may hold foreign-currency balances domestically or abroad without restriction. Profit remittance is unrestricted at transfer level, although dividends paid by a Swiss AG to non-resident shareholders attract 35% anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) which is fully or partially reclaimable under double-taxation treaties or refund procedures; no withholding tax arises on commercial re-invoicing payments for goods and services. ISIC 4690 general goods do not require import/export licences in Switzerland, subject to SECO lists on dual-use, sanctions and embargoes. The OECD classifies the Swiss franc as a freely usable currency with no Article XIV restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline, surrender ratio, or conversion obligation for export receipts or trade proceeds. The SNB only collects statistical data on cross-border payments through the bank reporting system; the remitter or beneficiary must truthfully indicate the transaction purpose (for example, goods payment or transit trade/commission business) in the SWIFT message. A Swiss company may keep collections in the original currency indefinitely; no central bank approval or conversion certificate is required for onward disbursement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital formation blocked account (Kapitalkonto) providing the bank confirmation for the Commercial Register; multi-currency operational settlement account in CHF/EUR/USD; trade finance and LC limits.
Multi-currency current account for operational clearing, cash concentration and direct SWIFT gpi payments; documentary and standby LC facilities.
Operational account with treasury deposits and FX execution for western Switzerland based entities.
SME operating and multi-currency account; suitable for domestic legal entities with a cooperative or SME profile; limited LC appetite.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: AMINA Bank AG (formerly SEBA Bank AG, Zug)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Digital-asset and stablecoin settlement account for optional XT-transfer crypto corridors; also supports fiat CHF/EUR/USD balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as primary treasury; Medium as a supplemental collection or disbursement rail. Legal constraints: taking public deposits in Switzerland requires a FINMA banking licence under Art. 1 of the Banking Act (SR 952.0); EU/UK EMI licences (for example Revolut, Wise or Qonto) do not passport into Switzerland, and an unlicensed EMI account cannot replace a Swiss bank account for substance or audit purposes. Approved overlay: a Swiss fintech-licensed entity (Art. 1b Banking Act; cap CHF 100 million public deposits, no interest allowed) may provide e-money wallets, and licensed EU EMIs may be used for EUR payouts in a pass-through structure where funds first settle in the Swiss licensed bank account and are then distributed via the EMI to small suppliers, provided KYC controls remain with the Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical onboarding interview is mandatory for at least one authorised signatory with Swiss domicile; Art. 708 CO requires at least one board member or resident representative with signatory power domiciled in Switzerland. FINMA-compliant video identification is accepted only for Swiss-resident or selected EU/EEA passport holders; non-resident UBOs and directors generally must appear in person or provide an apostilled, notarised identity file plus a successful video call, and many banks (particularly cantonal banks) decline accounts where no director can attend a Swiss branch in person. Practical standard: the Swiss resident director attends the account opening with original articles of association, Commercial Register excerpt, UBO declaration, organisation chart and valid passport; all other shareholders must be covered by corroborating bank reference letters and source-of-wealth records for high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficit: a one-director AG with an offshore parent and no Swiss workforce is treated as a letter-box entity under AMLA Art. 3(3) and the banking self-regulatory agreement VSB 2020, triggering enhanced due diligence or rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance proof package: Swiss lease agreement for a dedicated office at the registered address, contracts and payroll slips for local staff, proof of AHV/AN/ALV/BVG social security affiliation, genuine board minutes held in Switzerland, corporate email and telephone line on a Swiss domain, professional liability insurance, and a group structure memo demonstrating that contracting, invoicing, credit control and cash management are executed from Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or high-risk supply corridors (Southeast Asia, Middle East, or sanctioned-adjacent countries) where re-invoicing is used as a payment firewall.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate organisation chart from the ultimate parent company secretary; UBO declaration of all natural persons controlling 25% or more, signed in front of a notary; apostilled passport copies for each UBO; bank AML reference letters for upstream shareholders; list of final customers and suppliers with jurisdiction of incorporation; adverse-media and sanctions screening report (World-Check or Refinitiv) dated within 90 days of opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering risk: invoice values inconsistent with physical shipments, repeated discounting of trade receivables, or absence of logistics evidence for transit trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction audit file for the first three completed deals: master purchase and sales agreements, proforma and final invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or CMR/air waybills in a coherent Incoterms chain, insurance certificates, customs declarations for both export and import country, and a transfer-pricing memo confirming an arm's-length re-invoicing margin (typically 3-8% gross mark-up) with a bank undertaking that settlement occurs exclusively by bank transfer, SWIFT or documentary credit and never in cash.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Engagement with crypto-enabled rails (XT-Transfer or stablecoin settlement) and virtual IBAN providers with non-standard KYC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy restricting digital-asset rails to FINMA-recognised or equivalent FATF AML-regulated PSPs; confirmation that the Swiss entity holds the legal title to virtual IBANs; segregation of client funds statement from the platform provider; wallet address register with chain-analytics reports; valuation and tax data for any token positions; and an audit trail reconciling each stablecoin settlement to the underlying commercial invoice.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity: shareholders remit minimum paid-in capital of CHF 100,000 (nominal capital floor under Art. 632 CO; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid in) via SWIFT MT103 to the bank's capital-formation blocked account. Field 70 must state: 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital [amount] per Board Resolution dated [date]' and the bank codes the transaction for SNB statistics as direct investment/equity capital, since Swiss law prescribes no fixed purpose code registry. The bank verifies against the notarised articles of association and provides the capital confirmation for the Commercial Register entry; funds are released to the operating account only after registration of the AG as a legal entity. Subsequent shareholder loans must be supported by written loan agreements with arm's-length interest documentation and use a clear 'shareholder loan' remittance reference so no equity recharacterisation occurs for tax purposes, and no pledge or round-tripping of funds is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Open-account trade payments are executed by SWIFT MT103 with transaction referencing; documentary trade security via MT700 or MT720 letters of credit, MT707 amendments and MT760 standby LCs; the Swiss bank acts as issuing, advising or confirming bank depending on the corridor. Domestic CHF payments settle in real time over SIC (SIX Interbank Clearing); the EUR leg clears through SEPA/EUR-SIC connectivity; the Swiss payments industry is migrating to ISO 20022 MX formats. For XT-Transfer style virtual-account collection rails, the platform must confirm that funds are held with a licensed partner bank in the name of the Swiss AG, that balances are segregated and protected, and that the platform screens against Swiss SECO, UN and OFAC sanctions. KYC-deposit-side compliance requires every inbound credit to be matched against an issued invoice, with transport documents archived to prevent false-trade allegations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX outright forwards and swaps on freely convertible pairs (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF, EUR/USD) with maturities matched to the re-invoicing payment cycle
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for medium-term rebalancing of multi-currency treasury positions
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (puts and calls) on G10 currencies for asymmetric protection of trade margins

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted solely for restricted or non-convertible currencies of the trade book (CNY, INR, KRW, IDR, TWD, BRL) with settlement in CHF or USD, since CHF itself is fully convertible

Liquidity overlay and tenor-matched money market instruments (time deposits, treasury sweeps, and reverse repo collateralised by high-grade debt securities) under an ISDA/CSA master agreement with the Swiss prime bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval at general shareholders' meeting (Art. 698/699 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; shareholder resolution, audit report and minutes kept in corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date; for calendar-year accounts by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered remedy; mandatory dissolution proceeding under Art. 731b CO if unresolved; director personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of audited annual accounts with Commercial Register and SHAB publication (only if ordinary audit applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date; calendar-year filers due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive penalty up to CHF 5,000 per instance; warning notice; administrative strike-off in severe non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and Federal direct tax return (corporate income tax plus net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office of the registered seat and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March for calendar year; extension to 30 June generally granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 3% p.a.; late-filing fine up to CHF 10,000; deficiency penalty up to 30% of evaded tax for wilful misconduct

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each quarter; Q1 due by 31 May, Q2 by 31 August, Q3 by 30 November, Q4 by 28 February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4.5% p.a.; late-filing surcharge up to CHF 500; intentional evasion fine up to 30% of tax avoided and criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage declaration and AHV/AVS/ALV/BVG social security contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Office (SVA Zug) and pension fund appointed for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of the year following the payroll calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution default interest at 5% p.a.; administrative penalty; immigration restrictions against responsible directors for repeated unlawful employment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding tax declaration on dividends and other Swiss-source distributions (35% rate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which the distribution is made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; penalty up to 100% of unpaid withholding tax; personal joint and several liability of directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit mandatory if any two of three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million; turnover above CHF 40 million; average of 250 full-time employees. Simplified audit required for smaller companies; opt-out allowed only when fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and unanimous shareholder consent (Art. 727a CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b CO) applying Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS mandatory only for listed or authorised financial services entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO declaration to a public register exists in Switzerland. Ultimate beneficial owner identification is conducted under AML obligations (AMLA Art. 6) and documented internally, with written disclosure available to tax authorities or Commercial Register upon request. Transfers of registered shares require entry in the share register without delay; bearer share identification is confirmed by shareholders in advance of each annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (including bearer share entries)
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and board meetings
Accounting records and audited financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 900 - 2,500 per annum for domiciliation and administrative representation in Zug or Zurich
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 5,000 - 12,000 for simplified audit; US$ 15,000 - 30,000 for ordinary audit of a mid-size re-invoicing hub

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax combined effective rate in the Canton of Zug approximately 11.6%–14.9% depending on commune multiplier, with no statutory tax holiday for general re-invoicing trade; IP box and R&D super-deductions available only for qualifying intangible development, not for trading intermediation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return form (Formulaire cantonal pour personnes morales) per canton; federal tax return integrated; electronically filed via the cantonal tax authority's secure portal (e.g., ESTV / SwissTax / eTax interface, Zug: kantonzug tax portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is generally 6 months after the business fiscal year-end, with the 12-month period following the tax year as the ordinary filing window; extensions are available upon written request but interest on late payments accrues from the due date of the tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accurate description of the activity or purpose of the company according to the commercial register entry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the statutory purpose as registered; for a re-invoicing hub, state commercial intermediation and trade facilitation in goods without physical handling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal place of management and permanent establishment in Switzerland.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the registered seat in Switzerland; for a purely non-resident managed company not having a Swiss PE, the filing basis may be limited to Swiss-source income; ensure substance and management location are accurately disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit according to the commercial annual financial statements before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the audited or reviewed net profit; adjust for any non-deductible expenses, tax provisions, and transfer pricing corrections according to Swiss tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: taxes, dissipative expenditures, hidden profit distributions, excessive director remuneration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must identify any constructive dividend or re-invoicing margin adjustment resulting from transfer pricing audits; such add-backs trigger withholding tax at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: prior-year losses, participation relief, IP box deductions, and other allowable reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply participation relief only if the 10% shareholding or resale value threshold and holding period rules are met; loss carryforward is limited to 7 years and is forfeited upon change of control if a commercial restructure lacks economic justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income for federal, cantonal and communal purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with transfer pricing documentation and the approved arm's length gross margin; unsupported low margins or offsetting payments to related parties create audit risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity capital for capital tax assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report paid-in share capital, capital contribution reserves, and retained earnings; re-invoicing companies with high cash balances and low operational substance face disguised profit distribution risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss transfer pricing documentation declaration and intercompany transaction schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 170 (SIF) for advance pricing agreements; for a limited-risk distributor or mark-up re-invoicing hub, attach a functional and risk analysis and benchmark study.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to CHF 10,000 per tax period; procedural fines for incomplete records up to CHF 20,000; default interest on outstanding tax from the end of the tax year at the statutory annual rate, currently between 4.5% and 6.0%; tax evasion penalties of one to three times the evaded tax and potential criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source may apply if the non-resident parent is subject to a Swiss DTA and the Swiss paying agent has a valid withholding tax relief certificate from the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); otherwise, the standard procedure is: (1) file the Swiss withholding tax return on Form 110, (2) pay the 35% tax within 30 days of dividend distribution, and (3) the non-resident beneficial owner submits a Form R (CH/USA) or applicable treaty relief form to the Swiss competent authority to claim partial or full refund; a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the non-resident's competent authority attesting beneficial ownership and minimum shareholding qualification is mandatory for treaty application. The shareholder is required to demonstrate economic substance, substance over form, and absence of abusive treaty shopping under domestic anti-abuse rules and the principal purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty and interest withholding tax is 35%; however, royalties for intangible property used in Switzerland are exempt from the security-based withholding tax if the beneficial owner is a related company fiscally entitled to the tax relief; under most DTAs, interest rate is generally 10% reduced or 0% under the EU Savings-like provisions; royalties are typically 5% under the OECD-standard treaty rate, and qualifying parent-subsidiary interest and royalty payments may attract 0% under the EU-Associated States rules where the receiving company holds at least 25% of the paying company; anti-treaty-shopping rules and substance requirements apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 1,000,000 in aggregate intercompany transactions with a single related party in the tax year triggers contemporaneous local file and master file documentation requirements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations but applies substantive principles under the Swiss OECD-compliant tax framework, exchange of information standards, and the federal anti-abuse doctrine; a re-invoicing company must evidence a real economic employer, decision-making functions, business premises, qualified personnel (headcount and payroll), and risk-bearing capacity in Switzerland; a mere mailbox Administrative AG without local substance can be re-characterized as a shell or transparent conduit, leading to reclassification of income, denial of treaty and participation relief, and a 35% withholding tax leakage on deemed distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a materially false tax return, omitting income from re-invoicing transactions, maintaining off-book foreign accounts, or creating fictitious invoices to shift profit out of Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax prosecution under the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax and the cantonal tax acts; penalty of one to three times the tax evaded plus default interest; procedural fines of up to CHF 10,000; in serious cases a criminal fine of up to CHF 30,000 is possible; civil reassessment without a final time limit until tax is time-barred.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false filings may face imprisonment of up to three years (or longer for aggravated offenses), travel restrictions, seizure of personal assets, and joint and several liability towards the tax authorities for evaded tax in cases of culpable participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Re-invoicing transactions carried out at artificial margins that deviate from the arm's length principle, paying excessive commissions to an affiliated supplier, or failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation once the CHF 1,000,000 threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment of taxable income by the Swiss tax authorities, with a corresponding 35% withholding tax on the deemed constructive dividend or upward assessment; additionally, double taxation risk without a corresponding adjustment; administrative penalties of CHF 20,000 per documentation failure, plus late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and penalty if they have actively directed the transfer pricing policy and ignored documented warnings; social security and old-age pension insurers may initiate personal liability claims for abusively low margins that shortchange the Swiss social security system.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Re-invoicing hub organized with no employees, no office premises, all management decisions executed abroad, and purely passive flow-through of purchase and sale invoices without real commercial risk or operational function in Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may be disregarded as a transparent entity under Swiss practice and the OECD MLC anti-abuse approach; its income is reassessed as attributable to the foreign principal or beneficial owner; treaty and participation relief are denied; the withholding tax of 35% is applied on the entire distributed cash flow or deemed dividend; the competent foreign tax authority is notified through the Swiss exchange-of-information mechanism; liquidation or withdrawal of the Swiss registration may be ordered by the commercial register authority if the company lacks a real seat.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid withholding tax and social security funds under Swiss corporate law (article 757 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and article 12 of the Swiss Withholding Tax Act); they may suffer a personal travel ban to facilitate recovery, have their personal assets attached, and be subject to criminal prosecution for negligent money laundering if the entity's sole function is obscuring beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Tax Planning and Anti-Avoidance Rejection
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Circular re-invoicing arrangements designed solely to secure Swiss treaty benefits, repeated round-trip transactions among related entities in different tax jurisdictions, or using a Swiss conduit to hold equity or derive royalties without demonstrating the actual commercial substance of the re-invoicing trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Substance-based general anti-avoidance doctrine under Swiss case law (the Zweckverpflockung test) allows the tax authorities to disregard the legal form and assess tax based on economic substance; legal certainty rulings are denied; the resulting tax assessment triggers compound interest, penalties up to 100% of the advantage and criminal sanctions for qualified fiscal evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in a circular structure exposing the company to insolvency may be personally liable to the Swiss trade creditors for tort and to the tax administration for the amount of the fraudulent advantage; criminal courts may issue custodial sentences up to five years for aggravated fiscal fraud, plus confiscation of the economic benefit and a ban on holding director mandates in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Dividend Stripping Circumvention
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to a non-resident shareholder without filing and paying the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer), structuring dividend payments through a controlled shell to avoid withholding, or reclaiming a withholding tax refund to which no treaty entitlement exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid anticipatory tax from the debtors and all recipients of the distribution; penal surcharge of one time the evaded tax in case of negligence, up to three times in case of intent; criminal fines up to CHF 100,000 against the responsible organ; any unlawful refund claim is rejected and triggers a denial of all future relief certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board but not the administration is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax; they may face automatic lien on personal real estate in Switzerland, blocking of foreign travel and extradition for serious evasion; a criminal conviction in canton Zug may lead to a prison sentence of up to five years for the aggregate offence of fiscal fraud.
